facts.heading: Divorce after fifteen years
facts.content: Jana and her husband Radko decided on a divorce after fifteen years of marriage.
facts.evidence: After fifteen years of marriage, my husband Radko and I decided on a divorce.

facts.heading: Divorce conversation in September
facts.content: Radko told Jana in September that things couldn't go on like this.
facts.evidence: And in September he told me that it couldn't go on like this.

facts.heading: Jana's feelings after news
facts.content: Jana felt emptiness and anger alternating several times a day.
facts.evidence: Emptiness. And then anger. Then emptiness again.

facts.heading: Radko's reason for divorce
facts.content: Radko stated that they drifted apart and live next to each other.
facts.evidence: He says that we drifted apart. That we live next to each other.

facts.heading: Jana's self-blame regarding divorce
facts.content: Jana feels she should have seen the signs and is looking for where she made a mistake.
facts.evidence: I keep going over it in my head and looking for where I made a mistake.

facts.heading: Jana's uncertainty about cause
facts.content: Jana sometimes thinks she was too tired and didn't care, other times she cared too much.
facts.evidence: Sometimes I think I was too tired and didn't care about him, other times that I cared too much.

facts.heading: Jana's distress over children
facts.content: Jana is suffering mainly because of the children.
facts.evidence: Yes. And mainly because of the children.

facts.heading: Jana's children's ages
facts.content: Jana has two children: Anička who is twelve and Matěj who is eight years old.
facts.evidence: Anička is twelve and Matěj is eight years old.

facts.heading: Delay in telling children
facts.content: Jana and Radko are putting off telling the children about the divorce.
facts.evidence: Radek wants us to tell them together, but we keep putting it off.

facts.heading: Anička suspects fighting
facts.content: Anička asked Jana if Dad and she are fighting last week.
facts.evidence: Last week she asked me if Dad and I are fighting.

facts.heading: Jana lied to Anička
facts.content: Jana lied to Anička when she asked if her parents were fighting.
facts.evidence: Because I lied.

facts.heading: Jana's fear of telling children
facts.content: Jana is afraid of Anička's tears when telling her the truth.
facts.evidence: But I'm afraid of her tears.

facts.heading: Jana's desire for resolution
facts.content: Jana would like to get the divorce over with.
facts.evidence: I would like to get it over with.

facts.heading: Housing arrangements post-divorce
facts.content: The apartment is on a mortgage, and Radko is probably moving in with his brother.
facts.evidence: The apartment is on a mortgage. Radek is probably moving in with his brother, at least for now.

facts.heading: Children staying with Jana
facts.content: The children will stay with Jana.
facts.evidence: The children will stay with me.

facts.heading: Jana's concern about finances
facts.content: Jana is afraid she won't manage the situation alone because Radko always dealt with money.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid I won't manage it alone. Radek always dealt with money.

facts.heading: Job as Czech teacher in Brno
facts.content: Jana works as a Czech teacher at an elementary school in Brno. She teaches nine-year-olds and eight-year-olds.
facts.evidence: I work as a Czech teacher at an elementary school in Brno. I teach nine-year-olds and eight-year-olds.

facts.heading: Feeling life is falling apart
facts.content: Jana feels that everyone sees her life is falling apart.
facts.evidence: I have the feeling that everyone sees that my life is falling apart.

facts.heading: Principal knows about distress
facts.content: Only the principal at the school knows about Jana's situation.
facts.evidence: Only the principal. I told her

facts.heading: Principal gave early leave
facts.content: The principal allowed Jana to leave early, giving her an hour off.
facts.evidence: That she let me leave early. She gave me an hour off.

facts.heading: Worse when alone at home
facts.content: Jana felt worse when she was alone at home compared to being at work.
facts.evidence: But then I sat at home and it was worse.

facts.heading: Sleep waking at 3 AM
facts.content: Jana wakes up at three in the morning every night and thinks about the future.
facts.evidence: Every night I wake up at three in the morning and think about what will happen next.

facts.heading: Worries about finances/children
facts.content: When awake, Jana thinks about not having a mortgage or husband, calculates money, and imagines telling the children.
facts.evidence: That I don't have a mortgage, I don't have a husband, I don't have anything. Then I calculate the money, then I imagine how I will tell the children.

facts.heading: Sleep pattern duration
facts.content: Jana falls asleep around five and wakes up at half past seven.
facts.evidence: I fall asleep around five, and I wake up at half past seven.

facts.heading: Weight loss and appearance
facts.content: Jana has lost four kilos and a friend told her she looks terrible.
facts.evidence: I lost four kilos. A friend says I look terrible.

facts.heading: Support from sister Alena
facts.content: Jana has her sister Alena in Olomouc who calls her almost every evening.
facts.evidence: I have my sister Alena in Olomouc. She calls me almost every evening.

facts.heading: Support from friend Eva
facts.content: Jana has a friend Eva from work.
facts.evidence: And a friend Eva from work.

facts.heading: Tells Alena everything
facts.content: Jana tells Alena almost everything.
facts.evidence: Alena almost everything.

facts.heading: Tells Eva about difficult period
facts.content: Jana only tells Eva that she is having a difficult period.
facts.evidence: Eva only that I am having a difficult period.

facts.heading: Fear of failing as woman
facts.content: Jana fears that a woman who cannot maintain a marriage is not a good example for children.
facts.evidence: That a woman who cannot maintain a marriage is not a good example for children.

facts.heading: Belief from mother about marriage
facts.content: Jana's mother always said that marriage lasts no matter what.
facts.evidence: She always said that marriage lasts no matter what.

facts.heading: Mother's recent silence
facts.content: Jana's mother has not spoken much since telling her about the situation.
facts.evidence: She hasn't spoken much since then.

facts.heading: Desire for mother's hug
facts.content: Jana feels sad and wishes her mother would hug her.
facts.evidence: Sad. I would like her to hug me.

facts.heading: Family norm against showing need
facts.content: Jana believes expressing need is not done in her family.
facts.evidence: But that's not done in our family.

facts.heading: Finding relief in speaking out
facts.content: Jana finds that saying things out loud helps her a little.
facts.evidence: it helps a little.

facts.heading: Needs sleep and guidance

facts.evidence: Sleep. And knowing how to tell the children.

facts.evidence: Chamomile tea, and that's it

facts.content: Jana does not want to take the pills the doctor offered.
facts.evidence: I don't want them

facts.heading: Fear of missing children

facts.evidence: I'm afraid I won't be able to wake up in time for the children

facts.heading: Desire not to be dependent
facts.content: Jana does not want to be dependent on medication.
facts.evidence: And I don't want to be dependent

facts.heading: Agrees to paper journaling

facts.evidence: I could

facts.heading: Fear of panicking in front of children
facts.content: Jana is afraid she will panic and cry in front of the children.
facts.evidence: That I'll panic and cry

facts.heading: Fear of being unable to stay calm
facts.content: Jana is afraid she won't be able to stay calm.
facts.evidence: That I won't be able to stay calm

facts.heading: Worry about children's reaction
facts.content: Jana worries that crying in front of the children would be terrifying for them.

facts.heading: Anička is sensitive

facts.evidence: Anička is sensitive
